subject: Tenant-tailored retention: phased deletion playbook and evidence request
messages:
From: Aisha Ghosh <a.ghosh@stratumhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: m.barrett@stratumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify debug log TTL and phased deletion for pilot

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We kicked off an internal review of how Redwood retains tenant-scoped debug/audit traces for our pilot and have a couple of specific asks before we sign the pilot MSA: 

- Can you confirm the default TTL for per-tenant debug traces and whether that TTL applies to both streaming debug snapshots and persisted per-request traces?
- We need a tenant-scoped phased deletion plan: for pilot customers we want a 30/90/365 day phased approach (30d ephemeral for session-level traces; 90d aggregated debug artifacts; 365d metadata-only retention). Is that something Redwood can scope per tenant?
- Please provide a short sample of your "proof-of-delete" artifact for a sandbox tenant (hashes/timestamps) and the CAIQ/SSP section references we should map to that process.

Michael (security) is looped in. If you can send a proposed playbook and any supporting artifacts (high level matrix + sample proof), we can route to our compliance team.

Appreciate it,
Aisha
Security & Compliance, StratumHealth

---

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: a.ghosh@stratumhealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify debug log TTL and phased deletion for pilot

Hi Aisha / Michael —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise playbook and the artifacts we can share immediately. Attaching a retention matrix and a proof-of-delete sample for the sandbox tenant we used in the demo.

Quick answers up front:
- Default TTLs: session-level transient traces = 14 days (ephemeral by default), per-request debug traces persisted to the debug store = 90 days, metadata-only indexes = 400 days. These are our hosted defaults; all three tiers are configurable per-tenant for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Tenant-scoped phased deletion: we support configurable per-tenant policies and can implement your requested 30/90/365 window as a per-tenant profile. That profile will be applied at deployment time and can be changed via API with a 48-hour cooldown to prevent accidental mass changes.
- Proof-of-delete: we attach proof_of_delete_sample.txt (redacted) that contains the deletion job run id, timestamp, and SHA256 digest of the tombstone manifest for a sandbox tenant. We will demonstrate how to generate that digest from S3/Blob storage metadata.

Proposed phased-deletion playbook (high level):
1) Phase 1 (0–30 days): session traces kept ephemeral in-memory with optional short-lived persisted snapshots for debugging; retention policy: ephemeral=30d.
2) Phase 2 (31–90 days): move persisted traces to compressed debug bucket; index entries retained for 查找/traceback purposes; retention policy: debug_bucket=90d.
3) Phase 3 (91–365 days): purge payloads; keep metadata-only records (request id, timestamp, outcome) for 365d.
4) Proof-of-delete generation: daily deletion job produces a delete manifest + tombstone file; job writes to customer-specific audit folder and emits SHA256 digest with timestamp and job id.
5) Evidence and artifacts: we can provide a CAIQ mapping (see attached PDF) plus a short script that exports the manifest and computes the digest; optionally we can run the job in your sandbox org and deliver the artifact via secure transfer.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm acceptance of 30/90/365 as the pilot profile.
- We schedule a 30-minute compliance walkthrough with your security team (we'll have Kimberly join for CAIQ/SOC2 details).
- If agreed, we will run a proof-of-delete in your sandbox and deliver the artifact within 48 hours.

Attachments: retention_matrix_v1.csv, proof_of_delete_sample.txt, redwood_caiq_responses_v1.pdf

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify debug log TTL and phased deletion for pilot

Jasmine —

I'll join the compliance walkthrough. A couple of internal notes for the artifact we deliver so we stay on message with SOC 2 / SIG expectations: 
- Proof-of-delete artifact needs to include job id, timestamp (RFC3339), storage object keys deleted, and a signed digest (we use an HMAC with the key rotation id).
- For SIG/CAIQ we should point them to the specific control IDs covering data deletion and retention (we have mapped these in the attached CAIQ doc; highlight: CC6.1, CC6.2 equivalencies).
- Prio: include an explanation of how our KV cache TTLs interact with persisted debug traces so auditors don't conflate ephemeral cache eviction with permanent deletion.

I'll prepare the brief talking points and add them to the Drive link. Prio, please coordinate the sandbox job run and delivery.

—Kimberly
Director, Compliance Programs

From: Aisha Ghosh <a.ghosh@stratumhealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: m.barrett@stratumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify debug log TTL and phased deletion for pilot

Jasmine / Kimberly —

This is ✅ from our side in principle. A few clarifying points before we lock the pilot profile: 
1) Can the HMAC-signed digest be verifiable by us without a shared key (we prefer a signed digest using a rotated public key so Stratum can validate independently)?
2) For the 30d ephemeral tier: can we opt-in to a shorter in-prod window (e.g., 7d) for specific namespaces that process PHI, and have the API expose that per-namespace override?
3) We need to map the proof-of-delete outputs to CAIQ control IDs for our compliance intake — can you add a mapping table line-by-line in the CAIQ PDF?

If you can answer those three, we can proceed to the walkthrough. Also, please paste the HubSpot deal id here once you link the MSA so our procurement team can track.

Thanks,
Aisha

---

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: a.ghosh@stratumhealth.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify debug log TTL and phased deletion for pilot

Hi Aisha —

Great — answers inline below and next actions at the bottom.

1) Verifiable digest: we will provide an RSA-signed digest (2048-bit) for the deletion manifest using a rotating signing key whose public certificate we publish to a public endpoint. That lets Stratum independently verify without a shared secret. We will add the chain info and certificate thumbprint to the proof-of-delete file.

2) Per-namespace override: yes, the platform supports per-namespace retention overrides exposed via the Admin API. For PHI-flagged namespaces we can set a 7d ephemeral window and tag the namespace so the retention profile cannot be extended without an elevated approval workflow (audit trail included).

3) CAIQ mapping: will update redwood_caiq_responses_v1.pdf with a line-by-line mapping to the proof-of-delete outputs and to SOC2 control references. Kimberly will add the final callouts during the walkthrough.

HubSpot deal id: HS-43210 (we'll attach to the MSA and include in the walk-through notes).

Next steps:
- Kimberly and I will run a 30-minute walkthrough with your security team next week. Proposed slots: Tue 9/7 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 9/8 14:00–14:30 PT. Please confirm which works.
- On confirmation, Prio will run the sandbox deletion job and deliver proofs within 48 hours of the sandbox run.
- We will push an updated CAIQ PDF with the mapping and upload to the Drive link and HubSpot file area.

If you confirm 9/7 10:00 PT, we will send a calendar invite with an agenda and pre-reads.

Best regards,
Jasmine Liu
